title: Measuring Mechanistic Uncertainty in Large Language Models via Causal Robustness
abstract: arXiv:2610.22636v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in critical domains, where their susceptibility to hallucinations makes reliable and interpretable uncertainty quantification essential. We introduce the concept of mechanistic uncertainty, which characterizes uncertainty through the stability of the internal mechanisms supporting a model's response. We propose the causal robustness margin, defined as the minimum internal intervention required to deviate the model's output, and operationalize it using Jacobian Lens (Jlens) concept steering vectors. Across three open-source models and five question-answering datasets, we show incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins, indicating greater sensitivity to internal interventions, and the causal robustness margin complements conventional output-based uncertainty methods. Finally, in a controlled knowledge injection experiment, correctly learned facts show increased margins aft

translated_title: 通过因果鲁棒性测量大语言模型的机制不确定性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）在关键领域中的应用日益增多，其容易产生幻觉的特性使得可靠且可解释的不确定性量化变得至关重要。我们提出了“机制不确定性”这一概念，通过支持模型响应的内部机制的稳定性来刻画不确定性。我们提出了“因果鲁棒性裕度”，其定义为使模型输出发生偏离所需的最小内部干预量，并使用Jacobian Lens（Jlens）概念引导向量对该指标进行操作化实现。在三个开源模型和五个问答数据集上的实验表明，错误和不确定的响应表现出更小的裕度，说明其对内部干预更为敏感，且因果鲁棒性裕度与传统的基于输出的不确定性方法形成互补。最后，在一项受控的知识注入实验中，被正确学习的事实显示出更高的裕度。
tldr: 该论文提出“机制不确定性”概念及“因果鲁棒性裕度”指标，通过测量改变模型输出所需的最小内部干预量来量化大语言模型的不确定性，发现错误或不确定的响应裕度更小，且该指标与传统基于输出的不确定性方法形成有效互补。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of mechanistic uncertainty and proposes the causal robustness margin — the minimum internal intervention required to deviate a model's output, operationalized via Jlens concept steering vectors — demonstrating that incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins and that this metric complements conventional output-based uncertainty quantification.
